builder_plan.scenario: Tool errors or unavailable services cause your agent to abandon recoverable tasks.
builder_plan.change: Inject repeatable tool failures and change only the recovery policy.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retry and fallback behavior under the same injected failures.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Recovered tasks, duplicate side effects, retries, time to recovery, and total cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Cycle-of-Thought: Self-Evaluative Iterative Reasoning for Table Visual Question Answering in Document Images
summary: Replaces supervised fine-tuning and architectural changes for improving table VQA with a training-free, inference-time self-correction loop in which one VLM acts as generator, critic, and refiner. Costs linearly higher inference latency and token/API spend per query due to multiple model passes, though it avoids annotation and training cost. Can fail when the model's self-critique is unreliable, errors persist across iterations, or multiplied per-query cost outweighs the accuracy gain at production volume.
rationale: It is immediately usable with a single GPU or API access and no training, but the unquantified accuracy gain and linear inference cost increase require validation on the reader's own table VQA workload before production adoption.

claims.statement: Replaces supervised fine-tuning and architectural changes for improving table VQA with a training-free, inference-time self-correction loop in which one VLM acts as generator, critic, and refiner. Costs linearly higher inference latency and token/API spend per query due to multiple model passes, though it avoids annotation and training cost. Can fail when the model's self-critique is unreliable, errors persist across iterations, or multiplied per-query cost outweighs the accuracy gain at production volume.
Consistent accuracy gains on tabular VQA benchmarks, with small models (2B-7B) approaching larger-model performance; no multiplicative factor reported.
